author: high
claim: Every closed walk of odd length in a finite undirected graph contains a cycle of odd length.
evidence: Induct on the positive odd length m. If the closed walk has no repeated vertex other than its equal first and last vertices, it is itself an odd cycle. Otherwise choose an internal repetition and split the walk at the two equal occurrences into two closed walks whose lengths are positive, smaller than m, and sum to m. Exactly one of their lengths is odd; the induction hypothesis applied to that odd closed walk produces an odd cycle. Metadata: statement=Every odd closed walk contains an odd cycle; justification_type=logical_equivalence; confidence=1.0; is_fragile=false; fragility_reason=; suggested_followup=none; scope=global.

author: high
claim: If a finite undirected graph has no odd cycle, then in each connected component the parity classes of distance from a chosen root form a bipartition.
evidence: Choose a root in each component and classify each vertex by whether its shortest-path distance from that root is even or odd. If an edge had endpoints of the same distance parity, a shortest root-to-first-endpoint path, that edge, and the reverse of a shortest root-to-second-endpoint path would form an odd closed walk. The odd-closed-walk lemma would then produce an odd cycle, a contradiction. Thus every edge crosses the two classes. Metadata: statement=Distance parity gives a bipartition when odd cycles are absent; justification_type=by_definition; confidence=1.0; is_fragile=false; fragility_reason=; suggested_followup=none; scope=global.

author: high
claim: Every cycle in a bipartite graph has even length.
evidence: Fix a bipartition. Traversing any cycle, each edge moves from one part to the other, so vertices encountered after an even number of edges are in the starting part and those after an odd number are in the other part. Returning to the starting vertex can therefore occur only after an even number of edges.
